title: Comparison of extension by zero with the site morphism
statement:
Let $\nu_X:X_{\Proet}\to X_{\Et}$ be the comparison morphism of
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For an open immersion
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ and a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$ the
canonical comparison

$$
\nu_X^*j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!\nu_U^*F
$$

is an isomorphism for every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on
$U_{\Et}$, naturally in $F$ and compatible with composition of
open immersions; here the two $j_!$ are those of
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and
[def-weil-extension-by-zero].

proof.text: Write $r_j^{\mathrm{et}}=j^{\mathrm{et},-1}$ and $r_j^{\mathrm{pro}}=j^{\mathrm{pro},-1}$ for restriction. An open immersion is etale and etale morphisms compose, so every etale $W\to U$ also defines an etale $W\to X$. The etale inverse-image restriction lemma identifies $r_j^{\mathrm{et}}G(W\to U)$ with $G(W\to X)$, with the same restriction maps. Its identification is natural in the underlying abelian sheaf; applying naturality to each scalar endomorphism $\lambda_a$ ($a\in\Lambda$) shows that it is $\Lambda$-linear and gives the same identification for constant-coefficient module sheaves. For the specified sheafification construction of $j_!^{\mathrm{et}}$, the etale extension adjunction gives natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!^{\mathrm{et}}F,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,r_j^{\mathrm{et}}G)$. Its stated presheaf formula fixes the adjunction, including its counit, rather than choosing an unspecified left adjoint.

source.place: 03S2 (section-extension-by-zero), Definition 03S3 and following restriction and adjunction formulas

proof.text: Apply the current pro-etale localization lemma with $W=U$ and $A=\Lambda$: its open-immersion example supplies the site-object hypothesis. It identifies $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$, identifies the restriction of the constant ring sheaf $\Lambda_X$ with $\Lambda_U$, and states $r_j^{\mathrm{pro}}M(V\to U)=M(V\to X)$ with the module structure and restrictions inherited from $M$. The pro-etale extension adjunction states $j_!^{\mathrm{pro}}\dashv r_j^{\mathrm{pro}}$ for precisely the functor of [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Thus its Hom bijection is one of module morphisms. All restrictions here are localization restrictions; no geometric-stalk conservativity, quasi-compactness, or constructibility is required. Here the identification of sites is the canonical equivalence $\iota_j$, not a literal equality of independently chosen small skeleta. The section formulas and the later pasting calculations are made on the concrete bounded-object categories, where clause (1) states an isomorphism, and are read on the chosen skeleta through this equivalence. The coefficient identification is the unique ring map equal to the identity on constant sections, as in clause (2); hence two successive identifications and the direct one agree, since both have this defining property.

proof.text:
For fixed $F\in\operatorname{Mod}(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ put $A_jF=
u_X^*j_!^{\mathrm{et}}F$ and $B_jF=j_!^{\mathrm{pro}}
u_U^*F$. Using the two comparison adjunctions from the comparison definition and the extension adjunctions of steps 1 and 2, form the following bijections, natural in $F,M$:
$$ egin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}(A_jF,M)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_!^{\mathrm{et}}F,
u_{X*}M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,r_j^{\mathrm{et}}
u_{X*}M),\
\operatorname{Hom}(B_jF,M)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(
u_U^*F,r_j^{\mathrm{pro}}M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,
u_{U*}r_j^{\mathrm{pro}}M).
\end{aligned}$$
Postcomposition with $	heta_{j,M}$ between the rightmost Hom sets, followed by the inverse of the second chain, gives a bijection $\Psi_{F,M}:\operatorname{Hom}(A_jF,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(B_jF,M)$.

source.place: 09AF (lemma-jshriek-comparison), both functors left adjoint to the identified restriction functor

proof.text: Construct $\beta_F=\Psi_{F,A_jF}(\mathrm{id}_{A_jF}):B_jF\to A_jF$ and $\alpha_F=\Psi_{F,B_jF}^{-1}(\mathrm{id}_{B_jF}):A_jF\to B_jF$. Naturality of $\Psi$ in its target gives $\Psi_{F,M}(h)=h\circ\beta_F$ for every $h:A_jF\to M$; hence $\alpha_F\beta_F=\mathrm{id}_{B_jF}$. Naturality of $\Psi^{-1}$ under postcomposition by $q:B_jF\to M$ gives $\Psi^{-1}_{F,M}(q)=q\circ\Psi^{-1}_{F,B_jF}(\mathrm{id}_{B_jF})=q\circ\alpha_F$. Taking $q=\beta_F$ and using $\Psi^{-1}_{F,A_jF}(\beta_F)=\mathrm{id}_{A_jF}$ gives $\beta_F\alpha_F=\mathrm{id}_{A_jF}$. Thus $\alpha_F$ is an isomorphism. This specifies the canonical comparison in the displayed direction: it is the adjoint comparison corresponding to the sectionwise identity $\theta_j^{-1}$, equivalently the inverse of the mate $\beta_F$ of $\theta_j$. In particular its characterization is $\Psi_{F,M}(h)\alpha_F=h$ for every $M,h$; it fixes the map and not just existence of some isomorphism.

source.place: 09AF (lemma-jshriek-comparison), uniqueness of the adjoint, expanded using the natural Hom bijections

proof.text: For $f:F\to F'$, naturality in $F$ of $\Psi$ gives $\Psi_{F,A_jF'}(A_jf)=\beta_{F'}B_jf$. Naturality in $M$ gives the left side $A_jf\,\beta_F$. Therefore $A_jf\,\beta_F=\beta_{F'}B_jf$; multiplication by the inverses gives $B_jf\,\alpha_F=\alpha_{F'}A_jf$. This is the asserted naturality of the comparison in $F$.

For $V\xrightarrow{k}U\xrightarrow{j}X$, let $c^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,k}:j_!^{\mathrm{et}}k_!^{\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}(jk)_!^{\mathrm{et}}$ be the canonical etale composition comparison of the extension-composition lemma. On the pro-etale site, composing the two extension Hom bijections gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(j_!^{\mathrm{pro}}k_!^{\mathrm{pro}}H,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,r_k^{\mathrm{pro}}r_j^{\mathrm{pro}}M)=\operatorname{Hom}(H,r_{jk}^{\mathrm{pro}}M).$$
The last equality is the sectionwise identity of relocalization on the concrete bounded-object categories, including the coefficient identifications of step 2; on chosen small skeleta it denotes the corresponding natural identification. Two successive coefficient maps and the direct map agree because each is the unique ring map that is the identity on constant sections. Comparing this bijection with the Hom bijection for $(jk)_!^{\mathrm{pro}}$ and applying the explicit construction and inverse calculation of step 5 gives $c^{\mathrm{pro}}_{j,k}:j_!^{\mathrm{pro}}k_!^{\mathrm{pro}}\xrightarrow{\sim}(jk)_!^{\mathrm{pro}}$. The etale composition comparison is fixed by the identical construction with the etale extension Hom bijections and the sectionwise equality $r_k^{\mathrm{et}}r_j^{\mathrm{et}}=r_{jk}^{\mathrm{et}}$ from step 1. Thus on both sites precomposition by $c_{j,k}$ converts the composite-immersion transpose into the two successive transposes. These are the canonical adjunction composition maps: their transposes are identities of the iterated restriction functors. For the identity immersion the same prescription gives the unit identification; for three immersions either parenthesization transposes to the same identity on threefold restriction, so injectivity of the Hom bijection makes them equal.

proof.text:
For $F$ on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$, write $E_j$ and $P_j$ for the etale and pro-etale extension Hom bijections and $N_T$ for the comparison Hom bijection. The notation includes the source and target objects appropriate to each application. Step 4 says
$$\Psi_j=P_j^{-1}N_U^{-1}(\theta_j\circ -)E_jN_X.$$
First use the composite left adjoints, before applying $c^{\mathrm{et}}$ and $c^{\mathrm{pro}}$. For $h:\nu_X^*j_!^{\mathrm{et}}k_!^{\mathrm{et}}F\to M$, successively moving $\nu^*$ past $j_!$ and $k_!$ gives the Hom map
$$Q(h)=P_j^{-1}\bigl(\Psi_k(P_j(\Psi_j(h)))\bigr).$$
Substitution cancels the adjacent $N_U$ and $N_U^{-1}$ and gives
$$Q(h)=P_j^{-1}P_k^{-1}N_V^{-1}\bigl(\theta_{k,r_j^{\mathrm{pro}}M}\circ E_k(\theta_{j,M}\circ E_jN_X(h))\bigr).$$
Naturality of $E_k$ in its target says $E_k(\theta_{j,M}\circ t)=r_k^{\mathrm{et}}(\theta_{j,M})\circ E_k(t)$. Step 3 gives $\theta_{k,r_j^{\mathrm{pro}}M}\circ r_k^{\mathrm{et}}(\theta_{j,M})=\theta_{jk,M}$. Hence
$$Q(h)=P_j^{-1}P_k^{-1}N_V^{-1}\bigl(\theta_{jk,M}\circ E_kE_jN_X(h)\bigr),$$
which is precisely $\Psi_{jk}$ after the composition identifications of step 7. On the other hand step 5 gives $\Psi_j(h)=h\circ\beta_{j,k_!^{\mathrm{et}}F}$ and $\Psi_k(q)=q\circ\beta_{k,F}$; naturality of $P_j$ in its source then gives
$$Q(h)=h\circ\beta_{j,k_!^{\mathrm{et}}F}\circ j_!^{\mathrm{pro}}(\beta_{k,F}).$$
Evaluating these equal Hom maps at the identity, and inserting the composition maps, proves
$$\beta_{jk,F}=\nu_X^*(c^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,k,F})\circ\beta_{j,k_!^{\mathrm{et}}F}\circ j_!^{\mathrm{pro}}(\beta_{k,F})\circ(c^{\mathrm{pro}}_{j,k,\nu_V^*F})^{-1}.$$
Inverting this equation proves the required composition law
$$\alpha_{jk,F}=c^{\mathrm{pro}}_{j,k,\nu_V^*F}\circ j_!^{\mathrm{pro}}(\alpha_{k,F})\circ\alpha_{j,k_!^{\mathrm{et}}F}\circ\nu_X^*((c^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,k,F})^{-1}).$$
For an identity immersion, its extension adjunction identifies $E_j$ and $P_j$ with identity Hom maps, and step 3 identifies $\theta_j$ with the identity. Thus $\Psi_j=N_X^{-1}N_X$ and $\alpha_j$ is the identity under the unit identifications. All calculations use only naturality and inverseness of the established Hom bijections.
